node.label: Erving Goffman
node.date_label: 1959: The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life (Anchor US edition) · 1961: Asylums · 1963: Stigma: Notes on the Management of Spoiled Identity
node.description: A sociologist of face-to-face interaction and self-presentation. His account follows how participants infer, give and unintentionally disclose information, and how performances shape a shared definition of the situation.
node.representative_figures_and_works: The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life (Anchor US edition) (1959); Asylums (1961); Stigma: Notes on the Management of Spoiled Identity (1963).
node.scope_note: Selected theoretical contributions and dated texts, with original, revised, translated and posthumous forms distinguished. Source notes state actual reading extent; no complete monograph or comprehensive reception survey is claimed. Existing collective relationships and source/roster qualifications remain.

proposed_edges.relationship: Studies situated encounters through participants’ attempts to establish and manage a definition of the situation.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own introduction pp. 1–4 read; social inference and interactional responses are the object, not evidence that he founded practice-oriented historiography.

proposed_edges.relationship: Distinguishes intentionally given expressions from impressions others infer from expressions given off.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own introduction pp. 1–5 read. A specific resource for examining socially performed identities; not a claim of direct influence on all identity histories or an equation of tactical self-presentation with all diasporic identity formation.
